name: Panchadi Krishnamurthy killings
summary: Police detained Panchadi Krishnamurthy, the CPI(ML) secretary for Srikakulam, as he stepped off a train at Sompeta with six young comrades returning from Calcutta. They were taken into the woods and shot; the official version called it an encounter. The deaths broke the plains leadership of the Srikakulam Girijan uprising, the first rural armed campaign that carried the Naxalbari name into Andhra.
story: Most of the six were Boddapadu High School students in their teens. A CPI(ML) pamphlet a year later dated the shooting to 27 May.

casualties.claimedBy: CPI(ML) Sompeta area committee pamphlet; Shantha Sinha, Maoists in Andhra Pradesh
casualties.note: Police called it an encounter. Party accounts and later historians treat it as a custody killing after arrest at Sompeta station. Some theses give 24 May; the 27 May date is the usual anniversary.

reports.headline: Fatalities in Left-wing Extremist violence in Andhra Pradesh, 1968–2000
reports.excerpt: SATP’s Andhra compilation records 76 ‘terrorists’ killed in 1969, the year the Srikakulam leadership was broken in a string of police encounters.

reports.headline: The rise and decline of the Maoist movement in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
reports.excerpt: Uprisings in Naxalbari and Srikakulam in the late 1960s were suppressed. Since Srikakulam, ‘encounters’ have been commonplace in Andhra and Telangana.

name: Cossipore–Baranagar massacre
summary: On the night of 12–13 August 1971, Congress-backed vigilantes working with police moved through Cossipore and Baranagar in north Calcutta, pulling alleged Naxalite youths from houses. Later inquiry claims put the dead around 150, many of them teenagers, with bodies dumped in the Hooghly. The killings sit at the hard edge of the city’s annihilation years, when the word encounter entered Indian English.
story: West Bengal was under President’s Rule. A 1974 APDR-backed inquiry blamed a coordinated operation by security forces and Congress, with tacit help from a section of the CPI(M).

casualties.claimedBy: APDR / Haratosh Chakraborty commission tradition; The Wire 2020
casualties.note: No official contemporaneous body count. Inquiry and commemorative tallies cluster around 150; some accounts go to 200. Many of the dead were not armed cadres.

reports.headline: Why Mamata Is Sitting on Reports of Commissions Formed to Target Congress, CPI(M)
reports.excerpt: The Cossipore–Baranagar massacre of 12–13 August 1971 killed around 150 Naxalite activists and sympathisers, allegedly by Congress-aligned hoodlums in connivance with the police.

reports.headline: People’s tribunal sought for probe into 1971 massacre
reports.excerpt: More than 150 Naxalite youths were killed between 12 and 13 August 1971. Many bodies were dumped in the Hooghly. The carnage was masterminded during President’s Rule, allegedly by Congress vigilante groups supported by the police.

name: Alipiri bomb blast
summary: People’s War triggered a line of Claymore mines on the Tirumala ghat road just after Andhra Pradesh chief minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s convoy passed the Alipiri toll gate. His bulletproof car was thrown on its side; he walked out with a fractured collarbone. It was the closest a Naxal squad came to killing a sitting chief minister.
story: The jammer vehicle that usually led the convoy was not taken to Tirupati that day. PWG called the job the Alipiri Mission.

casualties.note: No deaths reported. Naidu, minister B. Gopalakrishna Reddy, and MLAs C. Krishnamurthy and R. Rajasekhar Reddy were injured. Rajasekhar Reddy was critically hurt.

reports.headline: A blast and its shock
reports.excerpt: On 1 October, People’s War activists triggered a series of nine Claymore mines on the ghat road to Tirumala, barely minutes after the chief minister’s convoy crossed the Alipiri toll gate. Naidu’s bulletproof car was hurled into the air.

reports.headline: Naxalite bomb attack on Naidu
reports.excerpt: Naidu escaped with a fractured hand and injured collarbone after landmine blasts sent his car off the road near Tirupati. Police said People’s War had planted claymore mines about 500 yards from the Alipiri entrance.

name: Koraput armoury raid
summary: People’s War squads walked into Koraput town after dark and spent about six hours looting the district armoury, police stations, the jail and the OSAP battalion. They left with hundreds of rifles and tens of thousands of rounds — a haul that armed the merger-era guerrilla force. A sentry died at the armoury; a mine on the Kolab road killed CRPF men covering the retreat.
story: The raid came seven months before People’s War and the MCC merged as CPI (Maoist). Cadres later said weapons were dumped in the Bastar forests.

casualties.sideLabel: police sentry, CRPF and Odisha police
casualties.claimedBy: SATP Koraput timeline February 2004; Times of India 7 Feb 2004
casualties.note: TOI contemporaneous: sentry killed at the armoury and two CRPF in a landmine, 11 injured. SATP: toll reached four with another injured policeman on 8 February.

reports.headline: Koraput (Odisha): Timeline of terrorist activities, February 2004
reports.excerpt: On 6 February two CRPF personnel were killed when PWG ambushed a truck near Kolab, and PWG shot a policeman at the SP’s office. By 8 February the casualty count in the Koraput attack had reached four.

reports.headline: PW extremists loot Koraput armoury; three killed
reports.excerpt: People’s War seized Koraput and decamped with over 1,000 guns. During the six-hour operation they looted the district armoury, five police stations and the jail, killed a sentry and blew a landmine that killed two CRPF jawans.

name: Jehanabad jailbreak
summary: About a thousand CPI (Maoist) fighters in police uniform took Jehanabad for two hours on polling night and opened the district jail. They walked their own cadres out — among them state secretary Ajay Kanu — and marched Ranvir Sena prisoners into the dark. Hundreds of other inmates simply left. It remains India’s largest jailbreak.
story: Pamphlets said Operation Jailbreak was timed to the November 1917 revolution, to rescue comrades and pass death sentence on selected Ranvir Sena men.

casualties.claimedBy: Rediff / PTI 14 Nov 2005; The Telegraph 14 Nov 2005
casualties.note: Telegraph split the siege dead as two policemen, two Maoists and two Ranvir Sena. Rediff put the night’s overall dead at about 12.
Nine hostages taken from the jail were reported killed the next day. Prisoner counts of those who walked out range from 341 to 389.

reports.headline: 18 years after India’s biggest jailbreak
reports.excerpt: On 13 November 2005 about 1,000 armed Maoists besieged Jehanabad jail, 70 km from Patna. Ajay Kanu, the reason for the break, walked out with 389 prisoners including Maoists and hardcore criminals.

reports.headline: Maoists storm Jehanabad jail
reports.excerpt: Naxalites stormed Jehanabad on Sunday night, killing at least 12 people. Dreaded Ajay Kanu, state secretary of CPI (Maoist), was believed to be among the escapees. Pamphlets called it Operation Jailbreak.

name: Errabore camp raid
summary: Hundreds of CPI (Maoist) fighters hit the Salwa Judum relief camp at Errabore before dawn, hacking and burning people who had been moved there from villages in south Dantewada. The camp was supposed to be a shield. It became a target. The raid is one of the named days of the Judum years, when Bastar’s war ran through roadside camps as much as through the forest.
story: Konta block is now in Sukma. In 2006 it was still Dantewada. Compensation files years later named 32 families.

casualties.claimedBy: Times of India 17 July 2006; SATP Dantewada July 2006
casualties.note: TOI same-day: 26, including three women and two infants. Hindu via SATP: 27 Salwa Judum activists. SATP 18 July: toll 33 after six abducted youths were found near Gaganpalli. Later compensation lists name about 32 families.
Police said four Naxals died in retaliatory fire. Not independently counted.

reports.headline: Dantewada (Chhattisgarh): Timeline, July 2006
reports.excerpt: Hindu reports put 17 to 27 dead at Erraboru camp on 17 July. On 18 July the toll rose to 33 after six kidnapped tribal youths were found near Gaganpalli.

reports.headline: Naxalites raid relief camp, kill 26 tribals
reports.excerpt: Three women and two infants were among 26 tribals killed as Naxals attacked the Errabore relief camp at Dantewada with firearms and sharp-edged weapons. Four Naxals were killed in retaliatory fire.

name: Rani Bodli raid
summary: A few hundred Maoists climbed the wall of an ashram-school camp at Rani Bodli with bamboo ladders, lit a generator, and threw petrol bombs into the barracks. When ammunition ran out, Chhattisgarh Armed Force men and Special Police Officers were forced into the open. Fifty-five died. It was the deadliest strike on a Salwa Judum-linked post before Tadmetla.
story: The outpost sat in a girls’ hostel. Three policemen who stayed awake in a separate wing lived. The officer in charge was suspended the next day.

casualties.note: PTI/Rediff: 16 CAF. Frontline later wrote 24 state police and 31 SPOs. The 16+39 split is the usual official count.
SPOs were Salwa Judum-era local militia on the state payroll. PTI: 39. Frontline: 31.

reports.headline: Maoists kill 54 policemen in Bastar, flee with weapons
reports.excerpt: Maoists killed at least 54 security personnel by attacking a police post at Rani Bodli in Bijapur. The raid, from about 2 a.m. to 5 a.m., saw grenades and petrol bombs before the camp was set ablaze.

reports.headline: Chhattisgarh: 55 killed in Naxal bloodbath
reports.excerpt: At least 55 police personnel were killed when more than 300 rebels stormed Rani Bodli. Sixteen Chhattisgarh Armed Force jawans and 39 special police officers died. The Naxalites looted 48 weapons.

name: Nayagarh armoury raid
summary: Several hundred CPI (Maoist) cadres in plain clothes took Nayagarh, 90 km from Bhubaneswar, and emptied the district armoury and the police training school. Simultaneous raids hit Daspalla, Nuagaon and Mahipur. Thirteen policemen and at least one civilian died. The guerrillas left with about 1,100 weapons in hijacked trucks and a bus.
story: Some of the raiders ate in town hotels before the shooting started, paid the bill, and made a short speech. Nayagarh is the hometown of then Odisha Maoist secretary Sabyasachi Panda.

casualties.claimedBy: Reuters / Nayagarh SP Rajesh Kumar 16 Feb 2008
casualties.note: SP Kumar: 13 policemen, including two women, mostly at the PTS, armoury and town station. Indian Express later used 13 policemen among 15 dead.
Reuters: one civilian. Express: a suspected informer and a village guard among those killed.

reports.headline: Naxals storm 3 police stations, kill 15
reports.excerpt: Fifteen persons, including 13 policemen, were killed in a siege of three police stations in Nayagarh. Maoists raided the town station and armoury about 10.30 p.m. and stormed the police training school.

reports.headline: Maoists kill 13 police in India's Orissa state
reports.excerpt: Hundreds of Maoist rebels attacked police stations in Nayagarh, killing 14 people and looting weapons. SP Rajesh Kumar said about 500 armed rebels rushed the town in vehicles and looted a huge quantity of arms.

name: Silda camp raid
summary: Maoists overran an Eastern Frontier Rifles camp in the Silda school compound in what was then West Midnapore. Twenty-four EFR men died in a raid the party named Peace Hunt, billed as an answer to Operation Green Hunt. It was the deadliest single day for security forces in Bengal’s Jangalmahal war.
story: Kishanji claimed the attack. Silda is now in Jhargram district. Early dispatches said 20 dead; the camp roll settled at 24.

casualties.claimedBy: The Hindu 15 Feb 2010; later camp roll
casualties.note: The Hindu’s first report said 20 jawans. Subsequent tallies and photo captions settled on 24 EFR, sometimes plus one civilian.

reports.headline: Maoists kill 20 jawans in West Bengal
reports.excerpt: Maoists attacked an Eastern Frontier Rifles camp at Silda in West Midnapore, killing 20 jawans in a raid later tied to the party’s ‘Peace Hunt’ against Operation Green Hunt.

name: Gyaneshwari Express derailment
summary: In the small hours, the Howrah–Kurla Gyaneshwari Express left the rails between Sardiha and Khemasuli. A goods train then smashed into the wreck. A hundred and fifty people died in their berths. West Bengal police and the CBI blamed a Maoist-backed PCPA sabotage of fishplates; Kishenji and the PCPA denied it. The attribution is still contested.
story: Railway minister Mamata Banerjee said there had been a blast. The DGP said clips and fishplates had been removed and forensics found no big explosion.

casualties.claimedBy: The Hindu 30 May 2010 (DGP 151, South Eastern Railway 148, district 145)
casualties.note: Attribution of the sabotage is contested: police/CBI/MHA blamed PCPA as a Maoist front; Kishenji denied CPI (Maoist) involvement; PCPA denied and blamed CPI(M). Mechanism (blast vs removed fishplates) was also disputed.

reports.headline: 79 killed as goods train rams Maoist-derailed coaches
reports.excerpt: A goods train rammed 13 derailed coaches of the Gyaneshwari Express between Khemashuli and Sardiha. Mamata Banerjee suspected a blast; DGP Bhupinder Singh said rebels had removed pandrol clips and fishplates.

reports.headline: Police: phone intercepts reveal Maoist hand in derailment
reports.excerpt: DGP Bhupinder Singh put the toll at 151; South Eastern Railway at 148; the district at 145. CID claimed intercepts showed Maoist squad members and PCPA supporters. Forensics found no evidence of a massive explosion.

name: Sarkeguda firing
summary: CRPF and state police opened fire on a night gathering of Adivasis from Sarkeguda, Kottaguda and Rajpenta, near Basaguda. Seventeen villagers died, several of them children. The force first called it an encounter. A judicial commission later found unarmed people sitting in an open field for a seed festival, and no Maoists.
story: Justice V. K. Agarwal’s report, tabled in the Chhattisgarh Assembly in 2019, called the police version false.

casualties.claimedBy: BBC 11 July 2012; Justice V. K. Agarwal commission 2019
casualties.note: CRPF first said all 17 were Maoists, then that civilians died in crossfire as human shields. The commission found unprovoked firing and no Maoists. Six CRPF were wounded; police said some wounds were from their own fire.

reports.headline: India police 'killed tribals, not Maoists' in Chhattisgarh
reports.excerpt: Rights activists said 17 people killed by paramilitary police in Bijapur on 29 June were local tribespeople, including a 12-year-old girl and school students, not Maoist rebels. Police first said all 17 were rebels.

reports.headline: It's plain slaughter in Bijapur: rights activists
reports.excerpt: A fact-finding team called the Sarkeguda firing a slaughter of unarmed villagers gathered from three hamlets, contradicting the CRPF encounter claim.

name: Latehar ambush
summary: CRPF and Jharkhand Jaguar companies walking in from Hehegara station were fired on from a hill in the Karmatiya forest. Eleven security men died in a day-long fight. The next morning villagers sent to lift bodies set off an IED packed under, or sewn into, a fallen jawan. Four of them died. The forest kept both the ambush and the trap.
story: Doctors in Ranchi later found a second IED stitched into another abdomen and defused it. Maoists said the bomb was meant for the force, not the village.

casualties.note: First-day reports said seven CRPF. The Hindu’s later ground reporting: 11 security personnel on 7 January. MHA Lok Sabha replies have used 10 CRPF plus one state policeman.
Early reports: two villagers killed in the 8 January blast. The Hindu later: four villagers died when they tried to lift CRPF jawan Baijnath Kisku’s body.

reports.headline: We were used as human shields in Latehar against Maoists
reports.excerpt: Eleven security personnel were killed in an encounter with Maoists on 7 January. Four villagers died in an explosion the next day when they tried to lift a CRPF jawan’s body. Villagers accused the CRPF of using them as shields.

reports.headline: Post-encounter, bodies of 7 CRPF men recovered; 2 more feared dead
reports.excerpt: Senior officials said nine security personnel from the CRPF and Jharkhand Jaguars may have been killed in Katiya forest on Monday. Two villagers helping retrieve bodies were killed when Maoists triggered a landmine.

name: Burkapal ambush
summary: A CRPF 74 Battalion road-opening party walking the Dornapal–Jagargunda stretch was boxed in near Burkapal. Twenty-five troopers of the Delta company died in a fight the force later compared with Tadmetla. It was the worst day for CRPF in Bastar since 2010, and it put Madvi Hidma’s south Bastar battalion on every briefing slide.
story: The same day is often listed as the Sukma 24 April 2017 attack. Kalapattar sits next to Burkapal on that road.

casualties.note: First Express headline used 26; the piece was updated to 25. CRPF listed 24 dead at the scene and one who died later.

reports.headline: Worst in Chhattisgarh in seven years: 25 CRPF men killed by Maoists in Sukma
reports.excerpt: Twenty-five CRPF personnel were killed in an ambush in Sukma, the worst day for the force in Chhattisgarh since the 2010 Dantewada attack. The party was on a road-opening patrol near Burkapal.

name: Gadchiroli nallah blast
summary: A Maharashtra C-60 quick-response team driving back from a morning operation hit a massive IED in a nallah near Jambhulkheda. Fifteen commandos and their civilian driver died. Gadchiroli is the western edge of the old Dandakaranya zone, a forest the war never treated as a border.
story: The blast came on Maharashtra Day. The unit had been out since dawn on a tip that a squad was moving near Lendhari nallah.

reports.headline: Many killed in Maoist attack in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli
reports.excerpt: Fifteen jawans and a civilian were killed when Maoists triggered an IED in Gadchiroli. The C-60 team was returning from an operation when the blast hit their vehicle in a nallah.

reports.headline: Gadchiroli Maoist attack: security personnel dead in IED explosion
reports.excerpt: An IED blast in Gadchiroli killed members of a police quick-response team. The attack was one of the deadliest Maoist strikes in Maharashtra in years.

name: Tekulagudem ambush
summary: A joint column walking out of Tarrem on the Sukma–Bijapur border ran into a PLGA battalion near Jonaguda and Tekulagudem. Twenty-two security men died — DRG, CoBRA, STF, Bastariya — in a four-hour fight along a two-kilometre stretch. Police said they had gone looking for Hidma. They found an ambush instead.
story: CoBRA commando Rakeshwar Singh Manhas was missing, then found alive in Maoist custody and later released. Police claimed a dozen or more Maoist dead; one woman cadre’s body was recovered.

casualties.sideLabel: DRG, CoBRA, STF and Bastariya battalion
casualties.note: Hindu: 22 recovered, one CoBRA still missing that morning (Manhas, later found alive). Split commonly given as 7 CoBRA and 15 Chhattisgarh police.
Police first claimed around 12 Maoists killed, later up to 20. One woman Maoist’s body was recovered. No independent count.

reports.headline: Sukma encounter toll touches 22; Shah, Baghel cut short poll campaigns
reports.excerpt: Bodies of 22 personnel were recovered after the encounter in Sukma; one commando was still missing. MHA adviser K. Vijay Kumar said Maoists had been trying to stop a road near Silger–Jagargunda.

reports.headline: Chhattisgarh encounter: 22 jawans killed in Maoist ambush in Bijapur
reports.excerpt: Twenty-two security personnel were killed and 30 injured in a gunfight between Jonaguda and Tekalguda on the Sukma–Bijapur border. The operation had been aimed at battalion commander Hidma.

name: Aranpur IED blast
summary: A District Reserve Guard vehicle hit a buried charge of more than 50 kg on the Aranpur road, barely a kilometre and a half from a police station. Ten DRG men and civilian driver Dhaniram Yadav were killed. Thirteen years after Tadmetla, Dantewada was still a place where a routine return from an operation could end in a crater.

reports.headline: Jawans killed in Dantewada Maoist attack
reports.excerpt: Ten jawans and a civilian driver were killed when Maoists triggered an IED in Dantewada. The blast hit a District Reserve Guard vehicle returning from an operation near Aranpur.

name: Kanker–Abujhmad encounter
summary: A joint column pushing into the Kanker–Narayanpur–Gadchiroli tri-junction reported killing 29 Maoists in the Binagunda–Hapatola jungle off Chhotebethiya. Police called it the first serious breach of Abujhmad, the ‘unknown hills’ that had been a closed guerrilla hinterland. Three security men were hurt. The dead, police said, included divisional committee members Shankar Rao and Lalita.
story: Fifteen of the 29 named by police were women. Independent verification of each identity did not follow the same day.

casualties.claimedBy: Chhattisgarh police / The Indian Express 16 April 2024
casualties.note: Police figure, including 15 women. Identities of named mid-level cadres were released by the force. No independent body count.

reports.headline: Maoist encounter in Bastar’s Kanker: security personnel, Chhattisgarh
reports.excerpt: Security forces reported 29 Maoists killed in an encounter in Kanker district on the edge of Abujhmad. Police said it was a major operation in a long-closed forest pocket; three personnel were injured.

name: Maredumilli encounter
summary: Andhra Greyhounds and other units reported killing Madvi Hidma, the south Bastar battalion commander named for Tadmetla, Jhiram Ghati and Burkapal, on a stream near Maredumilli in Papikonda. Police said his wife Madakam Raje and four guards died with him. For a generation of Bastar operations, Hidma had been the name on the other side of the ambush.
story: The party had already been squeezed out of much of Dandakaranya. The body was identified in Andhra, far from the Sukma roads he was said to own.

casualties.sideLabel: Madvi Hidma, Madakam Raje and four guards
casualties.claimedBy: The Hindu 18 Nov 2025; Andhra Pradesh police
casualties.note: Police named Hidma, his wife Madakam Raje, and guards Deve, Lakmal, Malla and Kamlu. Families later claimed the remains. APCLC and Maoist statements called the encounter staged; that claim is recorded, not settled.

reports.headline: Maoists killed in Alluri Sitarama Raju encounter
reports.excerpt: Andhra police reported six Maoists killed in an encounter in Alluri Sitarama Raju district, including the south Bastar commander Madvi Hidma, near Maredumilli.

reports.headline: Madvi Hidma, top surviving Maoist leader behind lethal attacks, killed in encounter
reports.excerpt: Hidma, named in the Tadmetla, Jhiram Ghati and Sukma ambushes, was reported killed with five others in the Maredumilli forests of Andhra Pradesh.
